clue.text: Course for foolish person rejected by army

indicators.note: by means next to, so the army abbreviation sits beside the turned word
something rejected is sent back, so the word for the fool is read backwards

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A fool is turned away by the army and sent on some kind of training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SAP into PAS. 'Course' looks like a training course; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is commonly served as one dish of a meal, such as a starter or main.

clue.text: Coming from abroad long before King George entered

indicators.note: entered means went into, so the letters for before and the king go inside the word for long

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn
ere is an old word for before
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: An immigrant who came long before King George's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' is the container signal; 'long' looks like an adjective of time but is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Peregrine originally meant foreign or travelling, from the Latin for a wanderer.

clue.text: Second choice as an oar

parts.note: a cull is a selection, a choice of animals picked out

explanation.surface: A substitute pick to serve as a rowing blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as an' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A scull is a light oar, one of a pair used by a single rower.

clue.text: Died on deck, holding up a lecture

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means placed beneath, so the other letters go below the A
on means placed above in a down clue, so D sits over the word for deck

parts.note: to deck is to adorn or dress up

explanation.surface: Someone died on a ship's deck, delaying a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck; it is the verb meaning adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech or talk given to an audience.

clue.text: Paddy took food, eschewing alcohol

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of rage, a burst of bad temper in British slang
ate means took food

explanation.surface: Someone in a rage had a meal but steered clear of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman; here it is British slang for a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate once specifically meant abstaining from drink, as in the temperance movement.

clue.text: Sound quality of certain lines, eventually

annotationWithheld.why: Sound quality of certain lines, eventually: lines = BR inside TIME, but 'eventually' (in time) must give both TIME and the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Sound quality of certain lines, eventually

clue.text: Nankin-Poo claimed to be the nomadic type

definitions.text: Nankin-Poo claimed to be the nomadic type

parts.words: Nankin-Poo claimed to be the nomadic type
parts.note: in The Mikado, Nanki-Poo sings that he is 'a wandering' musician, a travelling singer

explanation.definitionFit: A medieval travelling singer and entertainer wandered from court to court.

clue.text: No good among the Spanish, his strange tongue

indicators.note: among means the abbreviation for no good sits within the Spanish word

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters are made odd, jumbled

explanation.surface: A no-good fellow among the Spanish speaks an odd language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts NG in EL; 'strange' turns HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and this is the language of England.

clue.text: Ambitious person making rare visit

indicators.note: making means the letters are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A social climber pays an uncommon call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges RARE VISIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is an upstart, someone newly risen and pushing for status.

clue.text: Bird sounding to some like a noted princess

indicators.note: to some people's ears the word is pronounced the same as the princess's name

parts.note: Aida is the Ethiopian princess of Verdi's opera, noted as in set to music

explanation.surface: A bird whose call some think resembles a famous princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' means set to music, pointing to opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its down.

clue.text: Traveller distributing slices of bread?

parts.note: rounds are slices of bread, but a delivery man makes his rounds, travelling from door to door with goods

explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman doing a regular delivery route, such as a milkman or baker, travels a set circuit of houses.

clue.text: Show embarrassment at being stabbed

explanation.definitionFit: To go red is to blush with embarrassment, while one written word means pierced with a horn or tusk.

clue.text: One recalling information about aged dog

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for information goes round the word for old

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
old means aged
a retriever is something that recalls or fetches back stored information

explanation.surface: Someone who remembers facts about an elderly dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. 'One recalling information' suggests a person with a good memory, not a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden retriever is a popular breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Fools' precipitate entry, possibly

parts.note: alludes to the saying that fools rush in where angels fear to tread, a hasty charge through a door

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden flooding forward of water or people is a hasty entry.

clue.text: Came round and arranged further insurance

explanation.definitionFit: To come round after fainting is to regain consciousness; read as re-covered it means took out cover again.

clue.text: Odds on he's an American lawyer worshipping here!

parts.note: a bet is a wager at odds
he's gives the letters as written, ignoring the apostrophe
DA is a District Attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Someone bets that a US attorney is a church-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word. Bethesda is a common name for Nonconformist chapels in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a name given to many chapels, after the healing pool of the Bible, so it is a place of worship.

clue.text: Musical composition has lover in lead, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the old word for a lover goes inside the jumbled letters
perhaps hints the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: leman is an old word for a lover or sweetheart

explanation.surface: A piece of music features a lover in the leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the word lead to AL DE, and 'in' sets the lover between those halves. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An allemande is a stately German dance form used as a movement in baroque suites.

clue.text: Undeveloped island with grain beginning to emerge

indicators.note: with means joined to, so the pieces follow one another

parts.note: an inch is a small island in Scottish place names
oat is a cereal grain

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A small island where crops are just starting to sprout.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun and not yet fully formed.

clue.text: Special constable in East imitating Houdini

definitions.text: Special constable in East imitating Houdini

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for the constable is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
aping means imitating
SC is the abbreviation for special constable, a volunteer British police officer

explanation.surface: A volunteer policeman out east copies the great escapologist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Houdini was the famous escape artist, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was famous for getting free from chains and locked boxes, which is what imitating him involves.

clue.text: Peter the Republican, a real wildcat

parts.note: Peter Pan is J M Barrie's boy who never grew up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Republican politician called Peter is a genuine maverick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a real' is a link. A wildcat in politics is a maverick; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, usually a black leopard, living in the wild.

clue.text: Happened -to live with an popular doctor

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
Dr Fell is the man in the rhyme 'I do not like thee, Dr Fell'

explanation.surface: Someone happened to share a home with a disliked doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. The rhyme 'I do not like thee, Dr Fell' is an old English nursery verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell is an old-fashioned past tense meaning occurred or came to pass.

clue.text: Pen put in wrapper

explanation.definitionFit: To pen animals is to fence them in, and to put something in an envelope is to include it with a letter.

clue.text: Money from John's place?

parts.note: John o' ... is the far north-eastern tip of Scotland, whose last word names old silver coins

explanation.definitionFit: Groats were old English fourpenny coins, so a word for cash.

clue.text: Dairy product .made, Newton ever so rich, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters are put in an odd, jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
N is the scientific symbol for the newton, the unit of force
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton made a fortune, strangely enough, from something sold by the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' scrambles MADE + N + EVER SO RICH. Clotted cream from Devon is a classic topping for scones in a British cream tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted cream from the south-west English county is sold as a dairy product.

clue.text: Hidden order demanding retirement of boxer, say

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
go is a command telling someone to leave

explanation.surface: A secret instruction that a prizefighter must quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' looks like a fighter; it is the dog breed. 'of' is a link. To lie doggo is to stay hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying doggo is British slang for keeping still and out of sight.

clue.text: Heath's symphony — nothing less

indicators.note: less means without, so the letter for nothing is dropped

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Ted Heath's symphony, which amounted to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British prime minister who also conducted orchestras; here heath is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers.

clue.text: A yard, in King Arthur's day

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words King Arthur's

explanation.surface: A courtyard as it was in the time of King Arthur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'day' is a link word completing the surface. A garth is an old northern English word for an enclosed yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A garth is an enclosed courtyard or garden, often within a cloister.

clue.text: Like a female fighter in a riot by a river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river is placed beside the jumbled letters

parts.note: the Amazon is the great South American river

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters run amok into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman warrior caught in a riot near a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' scrambles IN A into IAN. The Amazons were a legendary race of women warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Amazons were a nation of women warriors, so the adjective describes a fighting woman.

clue.text: Make fewer bids, being unsystematic'

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means request less, while as one word it describes something lacking any pattern or arrangement.

clue.text: Directions are, sent back to cancel.

indicators.note: something sent back goes the reverse way, so the word are is read backwards

parts.note: S and E are south and east, two compass directions

explanation.surface: Orders are returned to be revoked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' gives ERA; 'Directions' looks like instructions, not compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub out writing is to delete or annul it.
